title: What If You Fired a Bullet Straight Up?

scenes.text: What if you fired a gun straight into the sky? The bullet's return trip is the real surprise.
A modern bullet leaves the barrel faster than sound, but air drag eats its speed all the way up.
At the top it stops dead for an instant, then falls back toward the ground.
Coming down, a .30 caliber bullet tops out near 300 feet per second, about 90 meters per second.
That is roughly a skydiver's speed. Anything from 200 to 330 feet per second can break human skin.
It never gets back to its muzzle speed, but it still hurts. In Puerto Rico, around two people die and 25 are hurt each New Year's Eve.

description:
What if you fired a bullet straight up?
It slows to a stop at the top, then falls at about 90 meters per second, enough to break skin.
What should we run through next?
